queries.query: large language model network configuration generation "intent to configuration" "network configuration synthesis"
queries.rationale: Locate papers and preprints on using LLMs to translate operator intent or NL into network configurations and automated config synthesis.
Find documented failure modes where LLMs produce incorrect or unsafe network configs (hallucinations, fabricated routes, invalid syntax).
Survey architectures that combine generation with automated validation and iterative repair for NetOps outputs.

queries.query: formal verification network configurations NetPlumber VeriFlow Batfish "configuration verification"
queries.rationale: Collect literature on deterministic and formal tools used to verify network configs, reachability, and policy conformance to use as validators or gold standards.
Identify NLP/ML techniques for constraining model outputs (constrained decoding, schema enforcement, type checking) that can be applied to NetOps.

queries.query: AIOps benchmarks network operations evaluation "NetOps benchmark" "AIOps" 6G-Bench TSNBench OpsEval
queries.rationale: Find existing benchmarks and evaluation suites aimed at AIOps/NetOps to assess validity and gaps for LLM-driven NetOps studies.

queries.query: dataset "network configuration" dataset topology configs "public dataset"
queries.rationale: Locate public datasets of network topologies, configurations, and policies suitable for experiments and reproducible evaluation.

queries.query: tool use retrieval-augmented generation RAG "LLM" "network" "knowledge retrieval"
queries.rationale: Search approaches that augment LLMs with retrieval/tool calls for up-to-date configuration syntax, policies, or topology facts to reduce hallucination.

queries.query: agentic network management autonomous agent "network operations" "automation agent"
queries.rationale: Survey agentic/autonomous frameworks for operational decision-making and orchestrated toolchains applied to NetOps.

queries.query: prompt sensitivity robustness "LLM" "network" adversarial prompts prompt engineering NetOps
queries.rationale: Identify studies on prompt sensitivity and adversarial prompting that affect output correctness in operational contexts.
Find literature on how domain mismatch and distribution shift degrade LLM performance and mitigation strategies (fine-tuning, adapter layers).

queries.query: human-in-the-loop verification network change workflows "operator" "approval" "human verification"
queries.rationale: Survey existing practices combining automated suggestion with human approval/validation in NetOps workflows and interfaces.
Search for program-synthesis and domain-specific language approaches (NetKAT, Frenetic) for config generation and formal guarantees.

queries.query: security risks network automation "misconfiguration" "LLM" supply chain attacks network automation risks
queries.rationale: Collect work on security threats introduced by automated NetOps, including adversarial misuse of LLMs and unsafe automation.

queries.query: evaluation metrics network correctness "reachability" "policy conformance" "syntactic validity" "semantic correctness"
queries.rationale: Identify metrics and validators used to measure configuration correctness and operational safety for quantitative evaluation.

inclusion_criteria: Works addressing LLMs or generative models applied to network configuration, NetOps workflows, or operational automation.
Papers, preprints (arXiv), tool documentation, and public datasets that provide reproducible artifacts (code, data, benchmarks).
Peer-reviewed conference or journal articles (SIGCOMM, NSDI, IMC, CNSM, USENIX), major ML venues (NeurIPS, ICLR, ICML, ACL) where methods are relevant.
Formal verification and validation tools and their primary publications (Batfish, NetPlumber, VeriFlow, NetKAT).
Industry case studies and vendor technical whitepapers if they include experimental data or reproducible methods.
Works in English; seminal older works included when directly relevant to methods or validators.
exclusion_criteria: Non-technical marketing pages or promotional material lacking experimental details or reproducible artifacts.
Blog posts or opinion pieces without citations or verifiable technical substance unless they point to primary sources.
Papers unrelated to network operations (pure NLP without operational application) unless they present generalizable mechanisms (e.g., constrained decoding) clearly transferable to NetOps.
Non-English sources (unless an English translation and verification are available).
Benchmarks or datasets behind inaccessible paywalls or with licensing preventing reproduction.
date_rationale: Emphasize literature from ~2020–2026 because rapid LLM and AIOps developments since 2021 are most relevant; include earlier seminal NetOps and formal-verification works (pre-2020) when they provide foundational validators, languages, or metrics (e.g., NetPlumber, NetKAT, Batfish).
